mainTopic: Dating a needle hole in the בית הכוסות, and when to worry about ריסוק אברים
overview: This עמוד starts by finishing a ברייתא about a needle found in the wall of the בית הכוסות. Blood on the needle means the hole was made before שחיטה, and a scab means the hole is at least three days old. The גמרא explains that missing blood proves something here only because a needle would have caught the blood. רב עוירא reports that רבי declared an animal טריפה with a needle on only one side. אביי gets the exact facts and finds that blood showed the hole went all the way through, so it is simply the משנה's case. Then the גמרא turns to ריסוק אברים, crushed limbs. It covers an animal found below a roof, רבינא's goat that jumped, a ewe dragging its legs, rams that butt each other, rams thrown by thieves, and stick blows to the back. The עמוד ends with רב נחמן's rule that being born does not cause crushed limbs, and רבא begins a supporting ברייתא that continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Blood on the needle tells us when the hole was made
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its rule: blood on the needle means the hole came before שחיטה. No blood means it came after שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: [If a drop of blood is found on the needle,] it is certain the hole was made before the slaughter. If no drop of blood is found on it, it is certain the hole was made after the slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא that uses blood on the needle to decide whether the hole was made before or after שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A living animal bleeds, so a hole made while it was alive leaves blood on the needle, and the animal is a טריפה. After שחיטה the blood stops flowing, so a clean needle means the hole came later and the animal is kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: It is certain / it is known

phrases.english: it is certain that it was before the slaughter;
phrases.notes: The first half of this sentence, about blood being found on the needle, is at the end of the previous עמוד.

phrases.english: if a drop of blood is not found on it,
it is certain that it was after the slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא begun before this section about a needle found in the stomach wall.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood on the needle means the hole came before שחיטה, so the animal is a טריפה. No blood means it came after שחיטה, so the animal is kosher.

steps.title: A scab shows the hole is at least three days old
steps.stepSummary: If a scab formed over the hole, the hole is at least three days older than the שחיטה. If there is no scab, whoever wants to take money must bring proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a scab formed over the opening of the wound, it is certain the hole was made three days before the slaughter. If no scab formed, the one who wants to take money from his fellow must bring the proof.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a second sign, a scab, which shows how long before the שחיטה the hole was made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A scab takes three days to form, so it proves the hole existed at least three days before the שחיטה. This matters when an animal was sold within that time and the buyer wants his money back. Without a scab we cannot know when the hole was made, so the buyer, who wants to take money, must prove his claim.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who wants to take money from another must bring proof

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how a medical sign can decide a money case, not only a question of כשרות.

phrases.english: If the opening of the wound formed a scab,
it is certain that it was three days before the slaughter.
If the opening of the wound did not form a scab,
the one who takes from his fellow bears the burden of proof.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second sign, the scab, to the blood sign from step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A scab proves the hole is at least three days older than the שחיטה. Without a scab, the person claiming money must bring proof.

steps.title: Why does missing blood help here but not for other holes?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a clean needle lets the animal stay kosher, when other holes make an animal a טריפה even without blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is different here from all other holes in the world, where even though there is no blood, the Master declares the animal a טריפה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges step 1. With ordinary holes, a lack of blood does not prove anything, so why should it help here?
steps.deeperAnalysis: With other holes, we do not assume the hole came after שחיטה just because there is no blood. So it seems odd that a clean needle should prove the hole came after שחיטה.

phrases.english: And what is different from all other holes in the world,
where even though there is no blood
the Master declares it a טריפה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule in step 1 that a clean needle means the hole came after שחיטה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's rule that no blood on the needle means the hole came after שחיטה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With other holes, missing blood does not save the animal. So why should it save the animal here?

steps.title: The needle gives the blood something to stick to
steps.stepSummary: With other holes there is nothing for blood to stick to. Here the needle would have caught the blood if the hole came before שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, there is nothing for the blood to stick to. Here, since there is a needle, if the hole had been made before the slaughter, the blood would surely have stuck to it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. A needle is a surface that blood clings to, so a clean needle really does tell us something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With an ordinary hole, any blood may soak back into the flesh, so missing blood proves nothing. A needle would hold onto blood from a living animal. So when the needle is clean, the hole must have come after שחיטה.
steps.whatToRemember: Missing blood is only a proof when something is there that would have caught the blood, like a needle.

phrases.english: There, there is nothing for it to stick to;
here, since there is a needle,
if it were so that it was before the slaughter,
the blood would certainly have stuck.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Missing blood should mean the same thing for every hole.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a needle catches blood, so only with a needle does missing blood prove the hole came after שחיטה.

steps.title: רב ספרא tells אביי about רב עוירא's report
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא tells אביי that a scholar from ארץ ישראל named רב עוירא reported that רבי declared an animal טריפה when a needle came out on only one side of the stomach wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא said to אביי: Has the Master seen this young Torah scholar who came from the West and said, 'My name is רב עוירא'? He said: A case came before רבי of a needle found in the thickness of the בית הכוסות, coming out on one side, and רבי declared the animal a טריפה.
steps.whatsHappening: A story begins. רב ספרא brings אביי a report about a ruling of רבי, and this sets up what follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא rules that the animal is a טריפה only when the needle goes all the way through, out both sides. רבי declared it a טריפה with the needle out of only one side, which seems to contradict the ברייתא. That clash is why אביי will want to hear the exact details.

keyTerms.meaning: The reticulum, the second stomach of a cow

steps.confusionAlert: This does not overturn the ברייתא. It is a report that needs clarifying, which is why אביי goes looking for רב עוירא.

phrases.english: Rav Safra said to Abaye:
Has the Master seen this young Torah scholar

phrases.aramaic: דַּאֲתָא מִמַּעְרְבָא, וְאָמַר: רַב עַוִּירָא שְׁמֵנִי,
phrases.english: who came from the West and said: Rav Avira is my name,
and he said: An incident came before Rabbi
of a needle that was found in the thickness of the reticulum
on one side, and he declared it a טריפה.
phrases.notes: The needle came out on only one side of the wall, not all the way through.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב סָפְרָא לְאַבָּיֵי חֲזִי מָר הַאי צוּרְבָּא מֵרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new story whose ruling seems to clash with the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי declared an animal a טריפה when a needle was found in the wall of the בית הכוסות coming out on one side.

steps.title: אביי goes to great lengths to reach רב עוירא
steps.stepSummary: אביי sends for רב עוירא, who does not come. So אביי goes to him, finds him on a roof, and climbs up himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי sent for him, but he did not come to him. So אביי went to him. He was standing on the roof. אביי said, 'Let the Master come down and come.' He did not come down, so אביי went up to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. אביי works hard to reach רב עוירא, which sets up the question he will ask next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי, the senior scholar, keeps giving way: first he travels to רב עוירא, then he climbs up to him. This shows how badly אביי wanted the exact facts of רבי's ruling.

phrases.english: He sent for him; he did not come to him.
phrases.notes: אביי is the one who sent. רב עוירא is the one who didn't come.

phrases.english: He went to him.
He was standing on the roof.
He said: Let the Master come down and come.
He did not come down; he went up to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story from step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling here. The story builds up to אביי's question.

steps.title: אביי asks for the exact facts of the case
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב עוירא to describe exactly what happened in the case that came before רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Tell me, the incident itself, how did it happen?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks for the precise details of רבי's case, so he can see whether it really contradicts the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer may hide in the details. Perhaps something about the case made it a טריפה even with the needle out of one side. אביי wants the facts before deciding anything.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֵימָא לִי גּוּפָא דְעוֹבָדָא הֵיכִי הֲוָה?
phrases.english: He said to him: Tell me, the incident itself, how was it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא לִי גּוּפָא דְעוֹבָדָא הֵיכִי הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The goal of the story: אביי finally gets to ask his question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact facts of the case of the needle that רבי declared a טריפה.

steps.title: רב עוירא describes the case that came before רבי
steps.stepSummary: רב עוירא explains that he was there when רבי saw a needle on one side of the בית הכוסות. רבי flipped it over, found a drop of blood on the other side, and declared it טריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I am the one who leads the gatherings, and I stood above the great רבי. רב הונא of ציפורי and רבי יוסי of מדי were sitting before him. A needle came before רבי that was found in the thickness of the בית הכוסות, on one side. רבי turned it over, found a drop of blood on it, and declared it טריפה. He said: If there is no wound there, where did the drop of blood come from?
steps.whatsHappening: רב עוירא answers אביי's question from step 7 and tells exactly what he saw. The needle showed on only one side, but there was blood on the other side too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story fills in a detail that the short report in step 5 left out. The needle did not come out on the outside, but a drop of blood was found there. רבי took the blood as a sign that the wound did go all the way through.

keyTerms.meaning: One who leads or directs the gatherings in the study hall
The reticulum, the second stomach of an animal that chews its cud
Thickness, meaning inside the wall itself

phrases.english: He said to him: I am a director of assemblies,
standing above the great Rabbi.
phrases.notes: "The great רבי" is רבי יהודה הנשיא. רב עוירא means he stood right near him, so he saw everything.

phrases.english: And Rav Huna of Tzippori
and Rabbi Yosei of Media were sitting before him,
and a needle came before Rabbi

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנִּמְצֵאת בְּעוֹבִי בֵּית הַכּוֹסוֹת מִצַּד אֶחָד,
phrases.english: that was found in the thickness of the reticulum, from one side,
and Rabbi turned it over
and found a drop of blood on it, and declared it a tereifa,
and he said: If there is no wound there,
where did the drop of blood come from?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's request in step 7 for the exact details of the case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly happened in the case before רבי.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The needle was on one side only, but a drop of blood on the other side showed a wound went through, so רבי ruled טריפה.

steps.title: אביי: this is just the משנה
steps.stepSummary: אביי complains that he went to all this trouble for nothing. The case is already in the משנה: a המסס or בית הכוסות pierced through to the outside is טריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: That man was troubled for nothing! It is a משנה: the המסס and the בית הכוסות that were pierced through to the outside.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that he knows the details, אביי says the ruling teaches nothing new. Since the blood shows the hole went through, it is the plain case of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The report in step 5 sounded like a big new חידוש: a needle on only one side makes the animal טריפה. Once the blood is added, the wound really did go through to the outside. That is exactly the משנה's case, so there is no new חומרא here.

keyTerms.meaning: He troubled him, meaning the effort was for nothing
The omasum, the third stomach of a cud-chewing animal

steps.whatToRemember: רבי's ruling is not a new rule about one-sided holes. The blood proved the hole went all the way through, which the משנה already calls טריפה.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: טְרָא טַרְיֵיהּ לְהָהוּא גַּבְרָא!
phrases.english: He said to him: That man was caused trouble for nothing!
phrases.notes: "That man" is אביי talking about himself. He climbed up a roof for this, as step 6 told us.

phrases.english: It is our mishna:
the omasum and the reticulum that were perforated to the outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to רב עוירא's details by placing the case under the משנה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The case before רבי was a full hole through the בית הכוסות, shown by the blood. So it is simply the משנה's case of a hole to the outside.

steps.title: רב הונא: an animal found below a roof is not suspected of crushed limbs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of an animal that fell from a roof. רב הונא rules that if you left it above and later found it below, you need not worry that its limbs were crushed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: one that fell from the roof. רב הונא said: If one left an animal above and came and found it below, we do not worry about crushed limbs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic from the משנה, an animal that fell from a roof. רב הונא limits it: if you did not see it fall, assume it is fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats a fall from a roof as a possible טריפה, because the limbs may be crushed. רב הונא says this only applies when we know it fell. If we only find it below, we assume it came down safely.

keyTerms.meaning: It fell from the roof, a case of possible טריפה in the משנה
Crushing or shattering of the limbs

phrases.english: It fell from the roof,
Rav Huna says:
If one left an animal above,
and came and found it below,
one need not be concerned about the shattering of limbs.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְלָה מִן הַגָּג, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new case in the משנה, the animal that fell from a roof.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal left above and found below, without anyone seeing it fall, is not suspected of crushed limbs.

steps.title: רבינא's kid jumps through a skylight: why is רב הונא lenient?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא's young goat saw barley through a skylight and jumped from the roof to the ground. רבינא asks רב אשי for the reason behind רב הונא's rule. Is it because an animal usually has something to grab on the way down, or because it judges the jump for itself?
steps.simpleTranslation: A young goat belonged to רבינא. It saw barley groats through a skylight and fell from the roof to the ground. They brought it before רב אשי. רבינא said to him: רב הונא's rule that an animal left above and found below is not suspected of crushed limbs: is it because it has something to grab on to, and this one had nothing to grab on to? Or perhaps it is because the animal judges itself, and this one also judged itself?
steps.whatsHappening: A real case comes up that tests רב הונא's rule. רבינא offers two possible reasons, and each one gives a different ruling for his goat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reason one: animals usually climb down holding on to something, so they don't really fall. A goat jumping through an open skylight had nothing to hold, so it would be suspect. Reason two: an animal only jumps if it judges it can land safely, and this goat also chose to jump, so it would be fine.

keyTerms.meaning: To grab hold of, to cling to
Or perhaps, introducing the second side of a question

phrases.english: There was a certain kid belonging to Ravina,
that saw barley groats through a skylight,
it fell from the roof to the ground,
they brought it before Rav Ashi.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָא דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא
phrases.english: He said to him: This that Rav Huna says,
"If one left an animal above and came and found it below,
one need not be concerned about the shattering of limbs":
is it because it has something to grab hold of,
and this one did not have anything to grab hold of?
Or perhaps it is because it evaluates itself,
and this one also evaluated itself?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses a real case to ask for the reason behind רב הונא's rule from step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is רב הונא's leniency based on the animal having something to hold on the way down, or on the animal judging its own jump?

steps.title: רב אשי: the animal judges the jump for itself
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that רב הונא's reason is that the animal judges whether it can jump safely. רבינא's goat also judged its jump, so it is fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is because it evaluates itself, and this one also evaluated itself.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי picks the second reason in רבינא's question. So the goat that jumped through the skylight is not suspected of crushed limbs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key is not whether there was something to hold on to. What matters is that the animal chose to jump. An animal that jumps on its own has judged that it can land safely. Only a real accidental fall raises the worry of crushed limbs.

keyTerms.meaning: It evaluated itself, judging that it could jump safely

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא's rule rests on the animal judging its own jump. So even an animal that jumped with nothing to hold on to is not suspected of crushed limbs.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is because it evaluates itself,
and this one also evaluated itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's question by choosing its second side.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for רב הונא's leniency.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The animal judges its own jump, so רבינא's goat is not suspected of crushed limbs.

steps.title: The ewe that dragged its hind legs
steps.stepSummary: A ewe in רב חביבא's house dragged its back legs. רב יימר said it simply had rheumatism.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a ewe in רב חביבא's house whose back legs dragged. רב יימר said: this animal just has rheumatism.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new story about a sick ewe, and רב יימר gives a simple explanation for its dragging legs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dragging legs could mean something serious that would make the animal a טריפה. רב יימר says no: it is only a common joint illness, so the animal stays kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: Rheumatism, a joint illness that makes walking hard

phrases.aramaic: הָהִיא אִימַּרְתָּא דַּהֲוָה בֵּי רַב חֲבִיבָא,
phrases.english: There was a certain ewe in the house of רב חביבא
whose hind legs would drag.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יֵימַר: הַאי שִׁיגְרוֹנָא נַקְטַיהּ.
phrases.english: רב יימר said: Rheumatism has taken hold of this one.
phrases.notes: Literally "rheumatism grabbed it." He means the dragging comes from a harmless illness.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא אִימַּרְתָּא דַּהֲוָה בֵּי רַב חֲבִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new case about whether to suspect a serious injury, after the story of רבינא's goat.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ewe dragging its hind legs is assumed to have rheumatism, not a deadly injury.

steps.title: רבינא suggests the spinal cord was cut
steps.stepSummary: רבינא challenges רב יימר: maybe the ewe's חוט השדרה was cut, which would make it a טריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא objected: But maybe the spinal cord was cut?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא pushes back on רב יימר's calm explanation and offers a more dangerous one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A cut חוט השדרה also causes dragging legs, and it makes the animal a טריפה. So רבינא is asking why we should pick the harmless explanation over the dangerous one.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat even if properly slaughtered

phrases.english: רבינא objects to this:
But perhaps the spinal cord was cut?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יימר's diagnosis.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יימר's assumption that the dragging is rheumatism
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same symptom fits a cut spinal cord, which would make it a טריפה, so why assume the harmless cause?

steps.title: The check proves רבינא right
steps.stepSummary: They examined the ewe and found its spinal cord really was cut, as רבינא said.
steps.simpleTranslation: They examined it and found it was just as רבינא said.
steps.whatsHappening: They checked the animal, and in this case the dangerous explanation turned out to be true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that רבינא's worry was not just theory, because it actually happened here. It sets up the surprise in the next step.

phrases.english: They examined her and found it as רבינא said.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבינא's objection with the real-life result.
steps.raayaObject: רבינא's suggestion that the spinal cord was cut
steps.raayaSupportSource: The physical examination of the ewe

steps.title: The הלכה follows רב יימר anyway
steps.stepSummary: Even though רבינא was right this time, the הלכה follows רב יימר, because rheumatism is common and a cut spinal cord is rare.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, the הלכה follows רב יימר: rheumatism is common, and a cut spinal cord is not common.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא decides the הלכה for the future: we go with the common explanation, even though the rare one happened in this story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is based on what usually happens, not on one unusual case. Since rheumatism is far more common, an animal with dragging legs is not treated as a טריפה without a reason.
steps.whatToRemember: We follow the common cause (rheumatism), not the rare one (a cut spinal cord), even after one case where the rare cause turned out to be true.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the check proved the הלכה follows רבינא. He was right about this one ewe, but the general rule still follows רב יימר.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a basic way the גמרא rules: practical law follows what is usual, not unusual exceptions.

phrases.english: And even so, the halacha follows רב יימר,
since rheumatism is common,
but a cut spinal cord is not common.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules against the result of the check in favor of the usual case.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: An animal dragging its hind legs is assumed to have rheumatism and is not a טריפה.

steps.title: Rams that butt each other
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא: rams that butt heads are not suspected of ריסוק אברים, even if they stand still in pain. But if they fall to the ground, we must worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: Rams that butt each other are not suspected of crushed limbs. Even if they are in pain and stand still, it is just a fever that has hit them. If they fall to the ground, we certainly worry.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives a new ruling about rams fighting, telling us when to worry about crushed limbs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Standing still in pain after a fight is not a sign of real damage; it is only a passing heat or fever. Falling to the ground is a sign of a hard blow, so then we must check for ריסוק אברים.

keyTerms.meaning: Crushing or shattering of limbs (makes an animal a טריפה)
We are concerned / we must worry

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: זְכָרִים הַמְנַגְּחִין זֶה אֶת זֶה –
phrases.english: רב הונא said: Rams that butt one another,
we need not be concerned about crushed limbs.
Even though they are in pain and stand still,
it is merely a fever that has seized them.
If they fell to the ground, we certainly are concerned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: זְכָרִים הַמְנַגְּחִין זֶה אֶת זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another ruling about when to suspect ריסוק אברים, continuing the theme of רב הונא's earlier rule about falling animals.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Butting rams are not suspected of crushed limbs unless they fall to the ground.

steps.title: Rams thrown by thieves
steps.stepSummary: רב מנשי: rams that thieves steal and throw over a fence are not suspected of crushed limbs, because thieves throw them carefully onto their hips so they can run.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מנשי said: Rams that thieves steal are not suspected of crushed limbs. Why? When they throw them, they throw them onto their hips, so that the rams can run ahead of them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מנשי rules that stolen rams are fine and explains why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason is the thieves' own interest: they need the rams healthy so they can run off with them. So they throw them gently and don't injure them.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב מְנַשֵּׁי: הָנֵי דִּכְרֵי דְּגָנְבִי גַּנָּבֵי –
phrases.english: רב מנשי said: These rams that thieves steal,
we need not be concerned about crushed limbs.
What is the reason?

phrases.aramaic: כִּי שָׁדוּ לְהוּ אַמׇּתְנַיְיהוּ שָׁדוּ לְהוּ,
phrases.english: When they throw them, they throw them onto their hips,
phrases.notes: The thieves toss the rams over a fence to get away with them.

phrases.english: so that they will run before them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מְנַשֵּׁי: הָנֵי דִּכְרֵי דְּגָנְבִי גַּנָּבֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another case of possible ריסוק אברים, this time from people throwing the animal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rams thrown by thieves are not suspected of crushed limbs, since the thieves throw them carefully.

steps.title: When thieves return the rams
steps.stepSummary: If the thieves throw the rams back, we must worry, but only if they return them out of fear. If they return them out of real תשובה, they will be careful.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they returned them, we certainly worry. That is only when they returned them out of fear. But if they returned them out of repentance, they have done complete repentance.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מנשי continues with the opposite case, when the thieves give the rams back, and adds a limit to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A thief returning rams out of fear no longer cares about them and may toss them roughly. A thief doing sincere תשובה is trying to make things right, so he returns them carefully and we need not worry.

phrases.english: If they returned them, we certainly are concerned.
And this applies when they returned them out of fear,
but if out of repentance,
they have done complete repentance.
phrases.notes: He means someone truly sorry will return the rams gently, so there's nothing to worry about.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reverse case of step 18 and then limits it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rams returned by thieves out of fear are suspected of crushed limbs; rams returned out of sincere repentance are not.

steps.title: A stick blow along the whole spine
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב: if a stick hits an animal lengthwise along the entire spine, from head to tail or tail to head, we don't worry about crushed limbs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: If one hit it on its head and the stick extended toward its tail, or on its tail and it extended toward its head, along the whole spine, we need not be concerned about crushed limbs.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives a base rule about an animal hit with a stick: a blow along the full length of the back is not dangerous.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the stick lies along the whole שדרה, the force is spread out over the entire spine. Because no single spot takes all the impact, nothing is crushed.

phrases.english: רב יהודה said in the name of רב:

phrases.aramaic: הִכָּהּ עַל רֹאשָׁהּ וְהָלְכָה לָהּ כְּלַפֵּי זְנָבָהּ,
phrases.english: If one hit it on its head and the stick extended toward its tail,

phrases.aramaic: עַל זְנָבָהּ וְהָלְכָה לָהּ כְּלַפֵּי רֹאשָׁהּ,
phrases.english: or on its tail and the stick extended toward its head,
along the entire spine,
we need not be concerned about crushed limbs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: הִכָּהּ עַל רֹאשָׁהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another case of possible ריסוק אברים, this time from a stick blow.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A stick blow running along the whole length of the spine does not cause concern for crushed limbs.

steps.title: Three stick blows that are dangerous
steps.stepSummary: We do worry if the stick ended in the middle of the back, if the stick had knots, or if the blow came across the back.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the stick ended at the middle of the back, we worry. If it had knots, we worry. If he hit it across the back, we worry.
steps.whatsHappening: רב finishes his rule by listing three kinds of stick blows that do cause concern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In each case the force lands on one point instead of being spread out: the end of the stick in mid-back, a knot sticking out, or a blow across the width of the spine. That focused force could crush the spine, so we must worry about ריסוק אברים.

keyTerms.meaning: Crosswise, like a slash across the width

steps.whatToRemember: A blow along the whole spine is fine. A blow ending mid-back, with a knotted stick, or across the back makes us worry about crushed limbs.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי שְׁלֵים חוּטְרָא אַפַּלְגֵי דְּגַבָּא – חָיְישִׁינַן;
phrases.english: But if the stick ended at the middle of the back, we are concerned.
And if it has knots, we are concerned.
phrases.notes: "It" here is the stick, even if the stick covered the whole back.

phrases.english: And if he struck it crosswise, we are concerned.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי שְׁלֵים חוּטְרָא אַפַּלְגֵי דְּגַבָּא – חָיְישִׁינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Lists the exceptions to the base rule in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A stick ending mid-back, a knotted stick, or a crosswise blow all raise concern for crushed limbs.

steps.title: Birth through the womb does not cause crushed limbs
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that passing through the בית הרחם during birth does not raise a worry of ריסוקי אברים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: The womb does not create a concern of crushed limbs.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן adds a new case to the list of things that do or do not cause ריסוק אברים. He says a newborn animal does not need to be suspected of crushed limbs just because it was squeezed out of the womb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the גמרא discussed outside forces like butting, being thrown, and being hit with a stick. Here רב נחמן deals with a natural squeeze that every newborn goes through. His ruling is that birth is not a danger of this kind, so a newborn is not treated as possibly having crushed limbs.

keyTerms.meaning: The womb, including the birth passage the newborn comes through
Crushed or shattered limbs, a possible טריפה worry
It does not carry a concern of / is not subject to

steps.whyThisMatters: Without this rule, every newborn animal would be in doubt about crushed limbs simply from being born.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
The womb does not have in it
a concern of crushed limbs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: בֵּית הָרֶחֶם אֵין בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם רִיסּוּקֵי אֵבָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another case to the series of rulings about when we do or don't worry about ריסוק אברים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Being squeezed through the womb at birth does not raise a concern of ריסוקי אברים.

steps.title: רבא brings a ברייתא that supports רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: רבא tells רב נחמן that a ברייתא supports his ruling, and begins quoting it with the case of a one-day-old baby.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב נחמן: A ברייתא was taught that supports you: A one-day-old baby...
steps.whatsHappening: רבא is bringing a proof for רב נחמן's ruling from a ברייתא. This line only sets up the proof: it starts the quote, and the rest of the ברייתא comes on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof will come from a case about a human baby only one day old. The idea is that if a ברייתא treats a newborn as healthy right after birth, that shows birth itself does not damage the body. The exact wording and how it proves the point continue after this line.

keyTerms.meaning: That supports you, a formula for bringing a supporting source
One day old, born just a day ago

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not finished here. Don't try to work out the proof yet; the rest of the quote comes on the next עמוד.

phrases.english: Rava said to Rav Nachman:
It was taught in a baraita in a way that supports you:
A one-day-old baby
phrases.notes: The quote continues on the next עמוד, so the sentence is cut off here.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַב נַחְמָן: תַּנְיָא דִּמְסַיַּיע לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings outside support from a ברייתא for רב נחמן's ruling in Step 22.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's ruling that the womb does not cause ריסוקי אברים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a one-day-old baby (the quote continues beyond this line).
